sections.content:
17,295 people

were counted on the census as "playworkers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Playworkers provide play opportunities for children in a range of formal and informal settings including play schemes, free play locations, and in pre- and after-school activities.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "playworkers" there were more women than men (88.5% compared with 11.5%).

This means "playworkers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 11.5% and women made up 88.5% of "playworkers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "playworkers" included:

  • educational support assistants
  • registered specialist nurses
  • housekeepers and related occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "playworkers", 13.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "playworkers" was 65 years or older.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "playworkers" included:

  • shelf fillers
  • fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)
  • kitchen and catering assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "playworkers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "playworkers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "playworkers", 14.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (87.2% compared with 12.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97%) than self-employed (3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
